risk.detail: The workflow graph and evidence validator jointly determine whether CI failures remain diagnosable and release-blocking.

observedIssues.fact: PR #408 run 30266670055 generated evidence inside template-smoke before downstream Jobs existed, while declaring all three Jobs required; validator diagnostics were conflated.
observedIssues.resolution: Moved generation to terminal ci-evidence with needs.*.result, complete job records, pre-failure validation, and separate diagnostics.

observedIssues.fact: Initial corrective startup created a skeleton before restricted workflow approval and final scenario/scope evidence were recorded.
observedIssues.resolution: Stopped implementation, completed Contract v2, recorded explicit user authorization, enabled restricted-write approval, and ran preflight/checkpoint before final verification.

observedIssues.fact: The first full ai-finish attempt stopped at quality-fast because the newly added orchestration test was not ruff-formatted.
observedIssues.resolution: Ran the repository formatter, reran quality-fast, and obtained a passing result; no test or quality threshold was weakened.

observedIssues.fact: Full quality found that the workflow graph change invalidated the committed candidate SBOM baseline, causing the supply-chain baseline regression to fail.
observedIssues.resolution: Added the generated SBOM, provenance, and release-digest paths to Contract scope; regenerated them with check_supply_chain and reran their checks successfully.

observedIssues.fact: After regenerating SBOM and provenance, full quality found that release.json still projected the previous supply-chain digests; a direct release-distribution check also demonstrated that the historical v0.5.42 metadata must not be promoted to a newer public identity inside this corrective Work Item.
observedIssues.resolution: Added release.json to Contract scope, updated only its SBOM/provenance digest projection, refreshed release-digests.json, and made the expensive distribution check conditional on explicit release-preparation intent while retaining release-state consistency for ordinary PRs.

observedIssues.fact: A reverse traceability audit found that Contract acceptance, scenario coverage, Summary evidence, and CI evidence documentation still described an earlier ordinary-PR subset design even though the user-authorized implementation requires a terminal aggregate over all three Jobs.
observedIssues.resolution: Before archive, aligned Contract, Summary, plan, documentation, and regression descriptions to the authoritative three-Job terminal aggregation design and removed the contradictory ordinary-PR subset fixture.

residualRisks.detail: The new aggregate graph still requires a hosted run to prove GitHub needs.result semantics and failure evidence persistence.
WI-21 must rebase and resolve any smoke workflow overlap before its performance claims are re-evaluated.
